title: Homogeneous and Bernoulli Equations
short: Change variables to reach a separable or linear equation.

blocks.html: Many nonlinear equations can be turned into ones we already know how to solve by a change of variables. The two classic families are homogeneous equations, which become separable, and Bernoulli equations, which become linear.

Homogeneous: if $y' = F\!\left(\frac{y}{x}\right)$, set $v = \frac{y}{x}$, so $y = vx$ and $y' = v + xv'$. Then $xv' = F(v) - v$ is separable.
Bernoulli: if $y' + p(t)y = q(t)y^{n}$ with $n \ne 0, 1$, set $v = y^{1-n}$. Then $v' + (1 - n)p\,v = (1 - n)q$ is linear.

A function of $y/x$ alone does not change if $x$ and $y$ are scaled together, so after writing $y = vx$ the right side depends only on $v$. The only place $x$ survives is the product rule term $xv'$, and dividing by $x$ separates the variables: $\frac{dv}{F(v) - v} = \frac{dx}{x}$.

blocks.title: A homogeneous equation
steps: Divide by $xy$: $y' = \frac{x}{y} + \frac{y}{x}$, a function of $v = \frac{y}{x}$: $F(v) = \frac{1}{v} + v$.
With $y' = v + xv'$: $v + xv' = \frac{1}{v} + v$, so $xv' = \frac{1}{v}$.

blocks.html: Divide $y' + py = qy^{n}$ by $y^{n}$: $$y^{-n}y' + p\,y^{1-n} = q.$$ The chain rule gives $(y^{1-n})' = (1 - n)y^{-n}y'$, so with $v = y^{1-n}$ the first term is $\frac{v'}{1 - n}$ and the second is $pv$. Multiplying by $1 - n$ leaves a linear equation for $v$.

blocks.title: The logistic equation as a Bernoulli equation
steps: Rewrite as $P' - rP = -\frac{r}{K}P^{2}$: Bernoulli with $n = 2$. Let $v = \frac{1}{P}$.
Then $v' + rv = \frac{r}{K}$, whose solution is $v = \frac{1}{K} + Ae^{-rt}$.
blocks.a: The familiar logistic curve from The Logistic Equation, found this time without partial fractions.

blocks.html: Common slips: substituting $v = y^{n}$ instead of $y^{1-n}$; substituting before dividing by $y^{n}$; and forgetting the factor $1 - n$ in $v'$. Also, dividing by $y^{n}$ hides the solution $y = 0$ (when $n > 0$). Check at the end by substituting your $y$ back into the original equation.

blocks.name: slopefield
blocks.cap: Slopes of $y' = y^{2} - y$ from the Bernoulli example. The blue solution $\frac{1}{1 + e^{t}}$ falls toward the equilibrium $y = 0$; solutions that start above $y = 1$ blow up.
